dEaecUuEqfc.summary: Ron Garret's Google Tech Talk argues that quantum mechanics is no harder to understand than relativity and that popular accounts wrongly rely on the Copenhagen interpretation. He presents measurement as entanglement and explains phenomena like the quantum eraser.
dEaecUuEqfc.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as the talk that finally made quantum mechanics click, especially for programmers.

dBnniua6-oM.summary: Robert Lustig of UCSF lectures on the biochemistry of sugar, arguing that fructose and lack of fiber drive the obesity epidemic via insulin. It is the widely viewed 90-minute talk that popularized the anti-sugar case.
dBnniua6-oM.why: The most-linked YouTube video on HN, recommended as an in-depth explanation of fructose metabolism.

d-7o9xYp7eE.summary: Regent Law professor James Duane gives startling reasons why people, even innocent ones, should always exercise their Fifth Amendment rights rather than talk to police. It is based on his article and book on the subject.
d-7o9xYp7eE.why: HN treats it as the canonical video to link whenever talking to police or interrogations come up.

d_zt3kGW1NM.summary: Anand Giridharadas presents his book Winners Take All at Google, arguing that the global elite's philanthropy and 'win-win' framing preserve the systems that create inequity. He challenges the audience, including Google employees, to examine their own role in that system.
d_zt3kGW1NM.why: HN commenters recommend it as a pointed critique of philanthropy and win-win thinking, delivered inside Google itself, and cite it across threads on wealth, tax and tech power.

d0nERTFo-Sk.summary: A rap battle in which John Maynard Keynes and F. A. Hayek debate the causes of boom and bust, stimulus, and bailouts. It was produced by Econstories to teach the two schools of thought.
d0nERTFo-Sk.why: HN recommends it as a funny, accurate and easy primer on Keynesian versus Austrian views of the business cycle.

dP1xVpMPn8M.summary: Russ Cox gives a 23-minute tour of the Acme text editor from Plan 9, showing its mouse-driven interface, executing commands from text, and its filesystem-based interface to other programs.
dP1xVpMPn8M.why: HN points people to it as the best introduction to Acme and its very different take on editors, shells, and GUIs.

d2lJUOv0hLA.summary: Episode 8 of the Fall of Civilizations podcast, a roughly two and a half hour history of the Sumerians. It covers their mysterious origins, invention of writing and mathematics, great early cities and eventual collapse, with myths, proverbs and recreated music.
d2lJUOv0hLA.why: HN commenters strongly recommend it as an audiobook-length, deeply informative introduction to Sumer and early Mesopotamian civilization.

dKx1wnXClcI.summary: Tantacrul dissects the UX and UI of Avid's Sibelius music notation software, going through a long list of bad design choices. The review is both a comic rant and a practical lesson in interface design.
dKx1wnXClcI.why: Recommended as the most entertaining serious critique of a software interface, and a crash course in UX mistakes.

dCuZkaaou0Q.summary: Guy Steele's invited talk at Clojure/conj on the informal metanotation computer scientists use in papers to describe languages. He traces how this notation developed and why it is often unspecified and arcane.
dCuZkaaou0Q.why: HN commenters recommend it whenever someone asks how to read type-system or CS notation in papers.

dljNabciEGg.summary: Howard Abrams demonstrates, in an EmacsConf 2015 talk, how he uses org-mode's Babel and Tramp to configure and operate remote servers from a single document. Code blocks, their results and the explanatory text all live together.
dljNabciEGg.why: HN people point to it as the best demonstration of literate devops, showing documentation and execution woven together in Emacs.

dK3zRXhrFZY.summary: Stefan Karpinski's European Lisp Symposium 2016 talk asks whether Julia is a Lisp. He covers the features it borrows from Lisp, such as macros and closures, and where it departs, including syntax and its type system, with generated machine code shown.
dK3zRXhrFZY.why: HN commenters recommend it as a brilliant talk on Julia's design and how it is or isn't a Lisp.

d8RRE2rDw4k.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that the Netherlands, famed for cycling, is also the best country for drivers. It explains how prioritizing walking, cycling and transit makes driving faster and more pleasant.
d8RRE2rDw4k.why: Recommended as the argument that better alternatives to driving also improve things for drivers, and as an introduction to Dutch urban planning.

dPHPNgIihR0.summary: Dan Olson of Folding Ideas critiques Fortnite's monetization, arguing it uses manufactured discontent, such as shop design and skins, to push spending. The video dissects the psychological techniques behind the game's business model.
dPHPNgIihR0.why: HN commenters cite it as the definitive critique of Fortnite's monetization and of manipulative free-to-play design.

db-7J5OaSag.summary: Brian Peiris demonstrates RiftSketch, a web app where you write JavaScript with Three.js while wearing an Oculus Rift and watch the world around you change live. It runs on Firefox builds with WebVR.
db-7J5OaSag.why: Repeatedly cited as an inspiring demo of what programming in VR could look like, which led some commenters to buy headsets.

d4EgbgTm0Bg.summary: 3Blue1Brown builds visual intuition for quaternions, showing how to think about this four-dimensional number system using stereographic projection and rotations in 3D space. It is part one of a two-part series with an interactive companion site.
d4EgbgTm0Bg.why: HN commenters recommend it as the best visual explanation of quaternions and a good way to visualize higher dimensions.

dW8Cy6WrO94.summary: The first lecture of N J Wildberger's History of Mathematics course, starting with Pythagoras' theorem and following Stillwell's text. It emphasizes the flow of ideas over proofs.
dW8Cy6WrO94.why: Recommended as an easy-to-follow math history course that gives perspective on the subject.

dGVqrGmwOAw.summary: Rich Hickey's long presentation on Clojure and concurrency covers locking and immutability, then goes in depth on refs, transactions and agents. It ends with a multithreaded ant colony simulation demo.
dGVqrGmwOAw.why: Seen as the definitive explanation of why traditional concurrency is hard and how Clojure's model addresses it, with some commenters crediting it with changing their careers.

da1vvigy5tQ.summary: Dr. Sarah Hallberg argues in a TEDx talk that type 2 diabetes can be treated and potentially reversed through diet, especially by restricting carbohydrates. TED flagged the talk as outside its guidelines and warned against taking it as medical advice.
da1vvigy5tQ.why: Commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of carbs, insulin and hunger, and several say it led them to try low-carb eating.

doaQC-S8de8.summary: An Every Frame a Painting video essay on how Akira Kurosawa used movement, weather and composition to tell stories. It draws on clips and interviews with other filmmakers.
doaQC-S8de8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a deeply researched example of film analysis and one of the most educational videos on YouTube.

d0yGdNEWdn0.summary: Chris Lonsdale presents a TEDx talk on how adults can learn a language in about six months, centering on immersion, comprehensible input and a practical learning methodology.
d0yGdNEWdn0.why: HN recommends it as an efficient, practical approach to adult language learning, with one commenter saying it changed their life.

d1EB1zsxW0k.summary: Bill Gates at Stanford's Global Energy Forum argues that cheaper solar, wind and storage are not nearly enough to stop climate change. He discusses natural gas, a carbon tax, nuclear, battery costs and the responsibilities of developing versus developed economies.
d1EB1zsxW0k.why: Cited in energy threads for Gates's argument on why batteries and renewables alone fall short and nuclear is needed.

dCSIXLIzhzk.summary: Cody's Lab builds a 200-billionth-scale model to show how far away the nearest stars are, using parallax and light speed. A short astronomy explainer on interstellar distances.
dCSIXLIzhzk.why: Recommended whenever threads need an intuition for the vast distances between stars.

dNs_kNilSjk.summary: Tech Ingredients shows how to make a homemade radiative cooling paint, with a custom liquid panel that cools below ambient temperature outdoors. The video covers the materials and how to apply the paint.
dNs_kNilSjk.why: HN points to it as an impressive, hands-on DIY demonstration of passive radiative cooling that works in practice.

dpw9EHDh2bM.summary: The first three talks from React Conf 2018, by Sophie Alpert, Dan Abramov and Ryan Florence. They introduce React Hooks and explain the problems with classes that hooks solve.
dpw9EHDh2bM.why: It is the canonical introduction to hooks, given by the people who built them, and HN uses it to answer questions about why hooks exist.

d6PyyatqJSE.summary: Rhonda Patrick interviews USC gerontologist Valter Longo about fasting, the fasting-mimicking diet, and their effects on longevity, cancer, and multiple sclerosis. They discuss mechanisms such as IGF-1 and autophagy and clinical trials.
d6PyyatqJSE.why: HN commenters recommend it as a deeper, more legitimate interview on fasting mechanics than typical diet content.

dcjkezf1ARY.summary: A seven-minute demo from the author of Notcurses, a C library for text user interfaces. It shows the 2.3.0 release, which adds Sixel and Kitty bitmap graphics integrated into its multiplane character-graphics model.
dcjkezf1ARY.why: HN people share it as a striking demonstration of how much graphics a modern terminal can do.

dqQw05Mr63E.summary: Oh The Urbanity! questions the framing that urban planning reforms like bike lanes and traffic calming wage war on suburbanites. It argues that suburban and urban residents alike want less traffic on their own streets.
dqQw05Mr63E.why: Cited in urbanism threads as a clear argument that car-dependent suburbs impose traffic on everyone.

drv3BP0Fdi8.summary: Clinical psychologist Stephen Ilardi argues depression is a disease of modern civilization and presents a lifestyle-based program to treat it without drugs. Topics include exercise, sunlight, omega-3s and social connection.
drv3BP0Fdi8.why: HN recommends it in depression threads as a practical, non-medication approach with concrete takeaways.

d0vY0CKYhPY.summary: Numberphile with Dr Holly Krieger shows how the digits of pi surprisingly emerge from the Mandelbrot set. A short, accessible math explainer.
d0vY0CKYhPY.why: Recommended whenever the Mandelbrot set comes up, as a neat and surprising result.

d3kfEeMZ65c.summary: A Google I/O 2013 talk by Android audio engineers on why reliable, low-latency audio is hard on the platform. It covers problem areas across the stack, platform work underway and techniques apps can use.
d3kfEeMZ65c.why: Treated as the definitive explanation of Android's audio latency problem, showing it spans the entire stack.

dF_9YcehCZo.summary: Bruce Waggoner of the Voyager team describes how engineers diagnosed Voyager 1's 2023 loss of telemetry and patched its flight software from 15 billion miles away. The talk covers the spacecraft's architecture and the scarcity of old documentation.
dF_9YcehCZo.why: Recommended as an amazing blind-debugging story with deep detail on 1970s spacecraft computing.

dFs9WO2B8uI.summary: An RSA Animate summary of Iain McGilchrist's lecture on the divided brain, arguing the brain's two hemispheres attend to the world differently and that this has shaped culture and society.
dFs9WO2B8uI.why: Recommended as an accessible animated introduction to McGilchrist's thesis on hemispheres and narrow versus diffuse attention.

dKJEpOtVgXc.summary: Sasha Rush surveys linear RNNs and state space models as replacements for attention in transformer-style models, in a talk for MLSys. It covers the foundational preliminaries and predates Mamba.
dKJEpOtVgXc.why: HN commenters recommend it for building intuition about state space models and the tradeoffs between transformer and SSM layers.

dXdoim96v5A.summary: Ben Eater writes a program in a made-up machine language and walks through the control logic an 8-bit breadboard CPU needs to execute it. It is part of his build-an-8-bit-computer series.
dXdoim96v5A.why: Recommended as the key video for understanding control logic and microcode.

djB9oK6pkbA.summary: Machine Thinking argues the 1751 machine, a metal-cutting lathe associated with Vaucanson, triggered the biggest explosion of wealth in history by enabling precise manufacturing of other machines.
djB9oK6pkbA.why: HN recommends the channel and this video as an explanation of how machine tools enabled modern manufacturing.

ds77e3aO9nA.summary: Kirk McKusick gives a narrative history of BSD from its start at UC Berkeley in the late 1970s through the 1980s releases and the lawsuit that led to 4.4BSD-Lite in 1992. It is full of anecdotes from a key developer.
ds77e3aO9nA.why: Recommended as an engaging, non-technical history of Unix and BSD from someone who was there, and cited for specific stories like the TCP/IP stack.

d6DBKoWbtjE.summary: Channel 4's George Clarke visits a council estate in Vienna and is surprised by amenities such as swimming pools and private TV channels. It showcases Vienna's high-quality social housing.
d6DBKoWbtjE.why: HN points to it as proof that government-provided housing can be attractive, in housing and homelessness threads.

dDddKmdLEdg.summary: A walkthrough of installing Synapse, Riot and Jitsi from scratch on Debian to run your own Matrix communication service. The description warns it is now quite outdated and links to updated material.
dDddKmdLEdg.why: Recommended as a practical demonstration that self-hosting a Matrix server is fairly easy, even on a small droplet.

d6iQrh2TK98.summary: Veritasium explores why the number 37 turns up so often, drawing on Tom Magliery's collection of 37 sightings and a poll of about 200,000 people asked to pick a random number. It covers how humans choose numbers and why 37 stands out.
d6iQrh2TK98.why: HN cites it in LLM randomness and number-picking threads as evidence that humans are also biased and predictable when asked for random numbers.

dPK6t7echuA.summary: Guy Steele's Strange Loop 2010 talk argues that programmers should not have to think about parallelism, and that languages should support algorithms built on independence and divide-and-conquer. He also recounts fitting a program onto a single punch card.
dPK6t7echuA.why: Recommended as a fantastic talk, valued both for its parallelism ideas and for the punch-card story.

dT9y-KQbqi4.summary: Joe Grand recounts being hired to hack a Trezor One hardware wallet and recover $2 million of cryptocurrency. He describes three months of experimentation, voltage glitching, failures and high-stakes attempts with only one chance to get it right.
dT9y-KQbqi4.why: Recommended as a gripping real-world hardware hacking story and a showcase of Joe Grand's skill.

dX649lnKAU0.summary: Technology Connections explains the early history of analog color television, from the 1954 start of modern color broadcasting, and how shadow masks work in CRTs. It is the first in a series on how analog color TV works.
dX649lnKAU0.why: HN commenters recommend it as an especially good explanation of analog TV and CRT shadow masks.

dngqR9gcDDw.summary: The first episode of Milton Friedman's 1980 Free To Choose series, on how markets and voluntary exchange organize economic activity and the price system. It includes visits to Hong Kong, the U.S. and Scotland and a panel discussion with critics.
dngqR9gcDDw.why: Commenters say it made market economics click for them and find it an interesting documentary relevant to welfare and UBI debates.

dw_mRaIHb-M.summary: Aamer Rahman of Fear of a Brown Planet delivers a stand-up routine on so-called reverse racism, arguing about power imbalance and why criticism of a dominant group is not equivalent to racism.
dw_mRaIHb-M.why: Pointed to as a comedic but clear explanation of power dynamics in discussions of race and diversity in tech.

d-YcVLq98Ew.summary: Scott Manley analyzes the idea of putting data centers in orbit, prompted by Lumen Orbit's funding. He examines the claimed advantage of constant solar power against launch cost, cooling and mass.
d-YcVLq98Ew.why: Recommended in orbital data center threads as a sober explanation of why the idea doesn't work out economically or thermally.

dGiQaabX3_o.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated overview of human origins and the vast prehistory before recorded history. It covers how modern humans emerged and spread.
dGiQaabX3_o.why: HN commenters recommend it as a compact, well-sourced intro to human evolution that even led one viewer to read Sapiens.

dQGnwKBxAKk.summary: Asianometry's short analysis of SMIC's N+2 node, China's 7nm leap forward. It considers how far behind the competition SMIC still is.
dQGnwKBxAKk.why: Recommended as a high-level, in-depth take on SMIC's 7nm progress and Asian chip manufacturing.

dX9CGRZwD-w.summary: Branch Education walks through a semiconductor fab and the dozens of steps used to turn silicon wafers into microchips, with 3D animation. It covers lithography, deposition and etching at a high level.
dX9CGRZwD-w.why: Pointed to as a clear visual reference for chip manufacturing steps.

d_FEaFgJyfA.summary: A BBC Earth clip from Super Powered Owls in which the team uses sensitive sound equipment to compare owl flight with other birds. It shows why owls fly almost silently.
d_FEaFgJyfA.why: Linked in owl-feather and quiet-flight threads as a clear audio comparison.

dfY5ZQDzC5s.summary: A short compilation of aircraft flying through clouds and moist air, showing the spiraling vortices that wings leave behind. The footage shows wingtip vortices and the way planes disturb cloud layers.
dfY5ZQDzC5s.why: HN commenters link it as a visual illustration of wingtip vortices and wake turbulence when discussing lift and aircraft wakes.

dmWQtI3DFFo.summary: Robin Deits presents the JuliaRobotics organization and shows how Julia is used to visualize, simulate and control a humanoid robot. The talk touches on real-time performance and composability across packages.
dmWQtI3DFFo.why: Julia fans point to it as a concrete example of Julia working for soft real-time robotics, especially when avoiding heap allocation.

doN4t5NKW-k.summary: In her final days as ISS commander, Sunita Williams gives an extensive tour of the station's modules and research facilities, narrating the work done aboard.
doN4t5NKW-k.why: Recommended as a great, understandable tour of life and equipment aboard the International Space Station.

doz1QJ7LwjA.summary: Dolly Parton's song Jolene, slowed down to 33 rpm so that it sounds deeper and more drawn out. The short clip is a well-known example of how pitch-shifting changes a song's mood.
doz1QJ7LwjA.why: HN people point to it as a slowed-down song that sounds more plaintive and haunting.

d2ogGZXmepY.summary: Doug DeMuro reviews the 2017 Chevy Bolt, which has a $37,500 base price and 238 miles of range. He looks at why it sells poorly next to the Tesla Model 3, noting its quirks and narrow seats.
d2ogGZXmepY.why: Cited as a thorough, candid review of the Bolt, particularly for its uncomfortable seats and uncool image.

dDsWTyLEgbk.summary: Grady Booch interviews John Backus, who led the IBM team that created FORTRAN in 1957, for the Computer History Museum in 2006. Backus describes the development of the first successful high-level language and its compiler. The interview runs 88 minutes.
dDsWTyLEgbk.why: HN recommends it because hearing pioneers explain early computing in their own words conveys the context and excitement of the era.

dlbMuv-jix8.summary: Lecture 1B of MIT's 6.001 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (1986) with Gerald Sussman, covering procedures, processes and the substitution model. It includes the line about the power of naming things.
dlbMuv-jix8.why: HN commenters hold it up as an unmatched introduction to programming and quote Sussman's line that knowing a spirit's name gives you power over it.

d-ruFmgTpqA.summary: AVweb's flight trial of Garmin's Emergency Autoland system, which flies a plane to a runway and lands it when the pilot cannot. It is part of Garmin's Autonomi automation on the G3000 avionics.
d-ruFmgTpqA.why: HN points to it as a concrete demo of emergency autoland when threads discuss pilot incapacitation and aviation automation.

d6Pcp944sRI.summary: NileRed tries to make a ring from pure purple gold, a gold-aluminium intermetallic that is brittle and hard to work with. The 53-minute video follows the chemistry and many failed attempts before he produces a finished ring.
d6Pcp944sRI.why: HN mentions it as a fascinating example of chemistry persistence and as something people learned from, such as discovering purple gold exists.

d8BcCLLX4N4.summary: Tom Scott visits IEX, a stock exchange that slows down trading with a long coil of fiber. The coil removes the speed advantage of high-frequency traders.
d8BcCLLX4N4.why: Cited as a quick, visual explanation of IEX's deliberate latency and of artificial delay as a fairness tool.

d99_h30swtM.summary: Tom Scott investigates moire-effect beacons, called Inogon leading marks, a Swedish invention from the 1980s that shows different patterns depending on the viewer's position. He visits one used to mark an undersea cable and tracks down its history.
d99_h30swtM.why: Linked as the accessible explanation of how moire navigation lights work.

dE-vOscpiNc.summary: NASA Goddard recreates the Apollo 8 Earthrise moment using Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data, narrated by Andrew Chaikin and synced with the astronauts' recorded conversation. It marks the flight's 45th anniversary.
dE-vOscpiNc.why: Linked as a visualization of how the famous Earthrise photo was taken.

dEv99vxKjVI.summary: A Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Elon Musk focused on Tesla Autopilot, covering the motivation for Autopilot and Musk's views on self-driving safety and autonomy.
dEv99vxKjVI.why: HN mostly cites it as a record of Musk's self-driving claims and timelines, often sarcastically in threads about missed FSD promises.

dF_-jQc53jw.summary: A short demo of Inferno, the Plan 9 descendant operating system, running on an Android phone as Hellaphone. It shows calls, SMS and data working. The video quality is rough because the camera was held in front of the screen.
dF_-jQc53jw.why: Shared as a demo of a minimal Inferno-based phone OS and an unusual dumb-phone approach.

daS5RHVAl2U.summary: EposVox reviews a very cheap USB 2.0 HDMI capture dongle sold under names like BlueAVS/Goodan, testing whether it works as an alternative to the Elgato Cam Link. He covers its quality and limits for webcam-style and camera capture use.
daS5RHVAl2U.why: Commenters cite it as evidence that a roughly $12-20 HDMI-to-USB capture device is good enough for many uses, such as digitizing video or using a camera as a webcam.

dcHEhO4J29U.summary: Peter Munch-Ellingsen explains at NimConf 2021 why he wrote his own keyboard firmware in Nim instead of using QMK or Arduino. He shows that the resulting firmware is very small.
dcHEhO4J29U.why: Pointed to as a real-world example of Nim in embedded work, mostly by the author himself.

dkZFtimgAcM.summary: Douglas Crockford's YUIConf 2012 evening keynote tries to explain monads in a way programmers can actually understand, in the context of JavaScript. He aims to break the 'monad tutorial curse'.
dkZFtimgAcM.why: Mentioned as a great talk alongside Crockford's book, and mostly quoted for his quip that once you understand monads you lose the ability to explain them.

dmeRQN9z504.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Andy Matuschak on how he learns, why memorization matters for understanding, and why most learning tools fail. The conversation also covers handling confusion and the role of tutoring.
dmeRQN9z504.why: Pointed to in threads on spaced repetition, tutoring and education as a thoughtful treatment of what effective learning requires.

dnHdqPBrtH8.summary: An Asianometry explainer on why the Soviet Union, once a leading computing power, fell far behind the US in computers by the 1980s. It traces the gap from the 1960s onward despite strong state support for science.
dnHdqPBrtH8.why: HN commenters cite it as a concise answer to why Soviet computing failed, including reliance on reverse engineering and bureaucracy.

dqwpQarrDwk.summary: Kurzgesagt explains the skyhook, a rotating cable with a counterweight that could catapult spacecraft from Earth orbit toward deep space. It covers why it would make space travel cheaper and more efficient.
dqwpQarrDwk.why: Used as the accessible reference for skyhook and space tether ideas in HN discussions of Mars transit, launch and space elevators.

dxk8b9rSKOo.summary: Amazon's Jon Jenkins at Velocity 2011 on how operations can drive revenue and on Amazon's highly available, autonomous architectures. It includes details on deployment frequency and Amazon's move to AWS.
dxk8b9rSKOo.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for facts such as Amazon.com running on AWS and its very frequent deployments.

d5wfMNNr3ak.summary: Dr. John McDougall argues at TEDxFremont that starch-based diets are what humans were born to eat, drawing on 40 years of nutrition and disease work.
d5wfMNNr3ak.why: Listed as one of several resources for high-carb, low-fat diets in nutrition debates, not heavily endorsed.

d6oBCYHzrTA.summary: Stephan Lagerholm of T-Mobile explains at NANOG how T-Mobile turned off IPv4 for over 10 million handsets using DNS64 and related technologies. He shares advice on finding and handling broken applications.
d6oBCYHzrTA.why: Cited as the primary source for T-Mobile US running IPv6-only mobile clients in IPv6 adoption debates.

d6sVWEu9HWU.summary: A demo of a Skyrim mod that uses Inworld AI to let players hold free-form conversations with NPCs. It previews LLM-driven characters in role-playing games.
d6sVWEu9HWU.why: Pointed to as an early example of LLM-powered NPC dialog in games.

dBqhIVyfsRg.summary: A Spike Jonze-directed Ikea commercial in which a discarded lamp is treated sympathetically, until a twist undercuts the sentiment. It is a short, well-known piece of advertising.
dBqhIVyfsRg.why: Used as the classic example of how easily humans anthropomorphize objects, brought up in AI and advertising threads.

dCud8H7z7vU.summary: A 2-minute scene from the film Amadeus in which the emperor says Mozart's opera has simply too many notes and Mozart asks which few to cut.
dCud8H7z7vU.why: HN quotes the scene humorously and analogically, for example about extremely dense Black MIDI music or whether melodies are scarce.

dEeyaAUCyZs.summary: A one-minute clip from the All Things D conference in which Steve Jobs says Apple is fundamentally a software company, with iPod, Mac and iPhone all being software. He says the hardware is where the money is but the value is in the software.
dEeyaAUCyZs.why: Quoted whenever someone needs Jobs's own words that Apple sees itself as a software company.

dFUlAQZB9Ng.summary: A clip from Jurassic Park in which Lex says, "It's a Unix system, I know this," while navigating a 3D file system view.
dFUlAQZB9Ng.why: HN commenters bring it up as a joke about ridiculous movie computing, though some note it was a real Unix file browser (FSN).

dKjCWfuvYxQ.summary: Corridor Digital's comedic fake video of a Boston Dynamics robot fighting back against its human tormentors, made with motion capture and VFX.
dKjCWfuvYxQ.why: HN brings it up only as a joke about robot uprisings and future AI overlords.

dQw4w9WgXcQ.summary: The official music video for Rick Astley's 1987 hit Never Gonna Give You Up, the song behind the Rickroll internet prank.
dQw4w9WgXcQ.why: HN mostly uses it as a Rickroll joke or as a stand-in test URL for tools handling YouTube links.

dSj6kvv7_Sg.summary: A NeXT, Inc. promotional video showing its highly automated factory and the manufacturing of the NeXT Cube, including automated circuit board assembly.
dSj6kvv7_Sg.why: HN cites it as evidence of early lights-out manufacturing and of Steve Jobs's factory automation roots in threads on automation and US manufacturing.

dTRKCXC0JFg.summary: A short clip of Inigo Montoya's line from The Princess Bride, 'You keep using that word. I do not think it means what you think it means.' It has no educational content beyond the film quote.
dTRKCXC0JFg.why: Commenters post it as a joke reply when someone misuses a word or term.

dWAO3vUn7nw.summary: Physics Girl compares hydrogen fuel cell cars and battery electric cars after driving 1800 miles in a Toyota Mirai. The video was part of a series sponsored by Toyota.
dWAO3vUn7nw.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of sponsored content, with critics calling it FUD about battery electric cars, though one commenter noted it as a comparison.

dWzz3NeDz3E.summary: Kitboga builds an elaborate automated phone maze with fake captchas, hold loops and absurd support to trap scammers for days. It also covers how this protects potential victims by wasting scammers' time.
dWzz3NeDz3E.why: HN discusses it as a creative scambaiting example, often for specific funny details like the scammer repeating the maze 127 times.

ddbxFi3-UO4.summary: Stephen Malinowski performs Bach's Little Fugue in G minor on organ, accompanied by an animated graphical score. Pedalboard playing carries one of the melodic lines.
ddbxFi3-UO4.why: Linked as the original organ version of the piece, with a visual score that makes the fugue easy to follow.

dht_3NziwSw.summary: A clip from Terry Gilliam's film Brazil in which the illegal heating engineer Harry Tuttle visits Sam Lowry to fix his heating problem.
dht_3NziwSw.why: Used purely as a joke reference to Harry Tuttle and the film's dystopian bureaucracy.

djV11Xbc914.summary: The official remastered 4K video for a-ha's 1985 hit, famous for its rotoscoped pencil-sketch animation blending live action and comic-book drawings. It won six MTV Video Music Awards in 1986.
djV11Xbc914.why: It is mostly a cultural touchstone on HN, cited for its sketch animation style or the song itself rather than recommended as something to learn from.

dk3oc1Hr62g.summary: A two-minute Google video of its self-driving car handling city street scenarios near the Googleplex. It shows the car dealing with cyclists, pedestrians, construction and a railroad crossing.
dk3oc1Hr62g.why: Cited as concrete footage of what Google's autonomous cars could do in 2014 when the feasibility of driverless cars was being debated.

dsx2vdn7gpY.summary: A very short clip of Bill Paxton's famous 'Game over man, game over!' line from the 1986 film Aliens.
dsx2vdn7gpY.why: HN users drop it as a joke or movie reference rather than as a recommendation.

dtjb2OhEQcU.summary: A short explainer from 2swap on the chaotic behavior of double pendulums. It examines how predictable the system is for some starting conditions and whether closed-form solutions exist.
